title: publish-release reports a present-but-unreadable credential as an absent one, sending the reader to the opposite remedy
description:
Measured during the 0.9.0 publish, 2026-09-18. The stored npm granular token exists in the login Keychain under service npm-opum-ai-publish, but reading it from a non-interactive shell returns:

  security find-generic-password -s npm-opum-ai-publish -w    exit 36  (errSecInteractionNotAllowed)

because the per-item ACL requires a prompt that a non-interactive shell cannot answer. findKeychainToken catches every security failure identically -- its own comment lumps together not found, wrong account, and security unavailable -- returns null, and resolveToken then reports:

  Auth: no stored token found (Keychain or NPM_TOKEN); falling back to the interactive npm login session. Each publish call will need --otp.

That message is not merely imprecise, it points at the opposite remedy. ABSENT means create and store a token. PRESENT-BUT-UNREADABLE means run security unlock-keychain at a terminal; there is nothing to create. A reader who follows the message goes hunting for a credential that already exists, and separately concludes that OTP is required when the token route needs none.

This is the same shape as QCLI-346, fixed the same night: one message covering two cases with opposite remedies, resolved toward the wrong one. There it was task_already_exists mapped to conflict; here it is every Keychain failure mapped to absent.

CONFIRMED REMEDY: after the owner ran security unlock-keychain, the same read returned exit 0 with a valid granular shape (length 40, prefix npm_, no whitespace) and the publish proceeded on the token route with no OTP at any point.

WIDER CONTEXT, from opum-agent (OPAG-265): the operator reports that lore-cli and quest-cli sessions repeatedly reach for OTP having forgotten the keychain tokens exist. lore-cli cause was different -- an absent entry on 2026-09-14, since fixed, with a stale record left un-amended. This repository cause is the ACL, and the fix here is to stop the tool reporting it as absence.

acceptanceCriteria.text: A Keychain read that fails with errSecInteractionNotAllowed (exit 36) is reported distinctly from an entry that does not exist, naming the service, the exit code, and security unlock-keychain as the clearing action.
The absent case still says what it says today -- create and store a token -- so the two remedies are never presented interchangeably.
A read failure that is neither of those (security unavailable, wrong account) remains distinguishable from both rather than being folded into whichever branch is nearest.
The exit-36 mechanism is recorded where a session looks at publish time, not only on this task -- the release runbook publish section and the repository profile.
The value of the credential is never logged in any branch, matching the existing guarantee.

plan: 1. findKeychainToken classifies security exit codes: 0 found, 44 absent, 36 locked (errSecInteractionNotAllowed), ENOENT unavailable, anything else unreadable with its exit code; never reads or logs the value on failure.

2. resolveToken carries that classification out; an exported describeNoToken() words each branch with its own remedy (absent: create and store a token; locked: security unlock-keychain at a terminal, nothing to create; other: the named failure).
3. The --otp-required refusal names the unlock remedy in the locked case instead of implying OTP is the fix.
4. Unit tests per branch in test/e2e/release/publish-release.test.ts, including that no branch prints a token.
5. Runbook publish section gains the exit-36 mechanism; the CLAUDE.md profile section already carries it and is updated to say the message is fixed.
finalSummary:
publish-release no longer folds every Keychain failure into "no stored token found". findKeychainToken now returns found / absent (security exit 44 or an empty value) / locked (exit 36, errSecInteractionNotAllowed) / unreadable (anything else, security missing included). resolveToken carries that state out, and describeKeychainState words each state with its own remedy: locked names the service, the exit code and security unlock-keychain, and says there is no token to create. Absent keeps create-and-store. Other failures read as "could not be checked" and are neither of those. A real publish with the entry locked and no --otp refuses with the unlock remedy. Only the found state carries the value, and no description includes it. The runbook publish section (state/remedy table) and the CLAUDE.md profile section record the mechanism; the CHANGELOG has an Unreleased entry. VERIFIED: bun run check exit 0 locally (653 pass), lore check exit 0; per-state tests in test/e2e/release/publish-release.test.ts; mutation disabling the exit-36 branch turned exactly the 2 predicted tests red and the other 16 green; on this host a missing service really exits 44. Delivered in opum-ai/quest-cli#270, CI run 36158525088 (Prepublication qualification, pull_request).
